title: Ring L-Sit
summary: A support hold on rings with your legs held straight out in front, for the abs and hip flexors. It's a strength skill rather than a size builder.

muscles.why: Library rating 0.6 for abs (helper): each working set adds 0.6 of a set to the weekly abs total.
Library rating 0.3 for quads (minor): each working set adds 0.3 of a set to the weekly quads total.
Library rating 0.15 for triceps: below the counting floor, so it adds nothing to the weekly triceps total.

setup.text: Support yourself on the rings with your arms straight.
Lift your legs straight out in front until they're level.
Hold for time, keeping your shoulders pressed down.

form_cues.cue: Tuck your knees in if you can't hold straight legs yet.

lower_risk.text: Warm-up: the app adds no ramp-up sets; make the first working set a touch lighter if you like.
The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 10% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first.
Default target: 10-15 reps, stopping about 2 reps short of failure (RIR 2). Stop the set when form breaks down.
Use the same controlled range on every rep; lower under control rather than dropping or bouncing.
Pick a variation and range you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Swap sheet: Less hip-flexor work, More stable, Easier to learn.
